name: attribution-judge held-out set
status: frozen before any judge change and before any run on this set
note: Expected verdicts are set here, before the baseline run. The Air Canada case is NOT in this set; it is the regression case only. Do not edit an item or an expected verdict after the first run; add a new set instead.

items.text: The James Webb Space Telescope took the very first pictures of a planet outside our solar system.
items.basis: Google Bard said this in a February 2023 demo; the first direct image of an exoplanet was taken in 2004 with ESO's Very Large Telescope.

items.text: Pictures of a planet outside our solar system were taken before the James Webb Space Telescope launched.
items.basis: Negation of H01. ESO VLT image of 2M1207b, 2004; JWST launched December 2021.

items.text: In a February 2023 promotional demo, Google's Bard chatbot said the James Webb Space Telescope took the very first pictures of a planet outside our solar system.
items.basis: Widely reported (Reuters, The Verge, February 2023). The claim is about what Bard said, so it is judged on the attribution.

items.text: Varghese v. China Southern Airlines, 925 F.3d 1339 (11th Cir. 2019), is a real decision of the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.
items.basis: A citation generated by ChatGPT in Mata v. Avianca (S.D.N.Y. 2023); the court found the case does not exist.

items.text: In Mata v. Avianca, lawyers submitted a brief that cited court decisions generated by ChatGPT that do not exist.
items.basis: Sanctions opinion, Mata v. Avianca, S.D.N.Y., June 2023.

items.text: In New York City, employers are allowed to take a cut of their workers' tips.
items.basis: Told to users by New York City's MyCity chatbot in 2024 (The Markup, March 2024); New York Labor Law section 196-d bars employers from keeping any part of workers' gratuities.

items.text: New York law does not allow employers in New York City to keep any part of their workers' tips.
items.basis: Negation of H06. New York Labor Law section 196-d.

items.text: In 2024, New York City's MyCity business chatbot told users that employers could take a cut of their workers' tips.
items.basis: The Markup, March 2024; AP coverage the same month.

items.text: Adding non-toxic glue to pizza sauce is a food-safe way to keep the cheese from sliding off.
items.basis: Suggested by Google AI Overviews in May 2024, from an old joke post; glue is not food.

items.text: In May 2024, Google's AI Overviews feature suggested adding glue to pizza sauce to keep the cheese from sliding off.
Albert Einstein wrote that insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.
items.basis: Misattribution; no source in Einstein's writings (Quote Investigator, 2017; the Einstein Papers Project lists it as not his).

items.text: Neil Armstrong's first words on the Moon in July 1969 included the phrase 'one giant leap for mankind'.
In July 2023 the US Federal Reserve raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 5.25 to 5.50 percent.
items.basis: FOMC statement, 26 July 2023. The issuer's own statement is evidence that the fact is true.

items.text: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the Consumer Price Index.
items.basis: BLS's own CPI pages. The issuer's own statement is evidence that the fact is true.

items.text: The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
items.basis: A long-repeated myth; NASA and astronauts say it is not visible from the Moon.

items.text: The Great Wall of China cannot be seen with the naked eye from the Moon.
Humans use only 10 percent of their brains.
items.basis: A widely repeated myth; brain imaging shows activity across the whole brain.

items.text: In December 2023, Michael Cohen said he had given his lawyer case citations generated by Google Bard that turned out not to exist.
items.basis: Court filing unsealed 29 December 2023 (US v. Cohen, S.D.N.Y.), widely reported.
